modelName: CT unwrapped-diagram and SSPz geometry reference
purpose: Visualize how angular-longitudinal candidate geometry can affect configured-output SSPz by applying an idealized fan-beam 180LI acquisition-geometry explanatory model. The acquired complementary views bracketing beta plus 180 degrees plus 2 gamma are each combined with the direct view for longitudinal nearest-bracketing interpolation, and the two angular branches are then linearly interpolated. The reader-facing geometry indicator is the unweighted population standard deviation, in millimetres, of all detector-row centre positions in the direct acquired view and in each distinct acquired view bracketing the ideal complementary angle. It is evaluated before candidate selection, interpolation weighting, row-aperture modelling, and configured slice thickness. The earlier direct-ray 0-to-360-degree full-scan model remains available as a comparator.

referenceImplementation.note: The primary explanatory SSPz calculation applies the web model's fan-beam 180LI acquisition geometry. For every direct acquired view, it derives the ideal complementary angle, retains the two acquired angular neighbors, performs longitudinal nearest-bracketing interpolation over the union of direct- and complementary-side detector rows for each branch, and linearly combines the branches. Candidate row apertures are rasterized by exact fractional overlap with z cells, and configured-thickness averaging exactly integrates the resulting piecewise-constant cells. The original actual-data-only 360-degree path is retained as an explicit comparator. This is not a reproduction of scanner-specific projection selection, redundancy weighting, z filtering, cone-beam weighting, or backprojection.

scanCalculationConvention: The default path evaluates every direct acquired view beta in the half-open interval 0 <= beta < 360 degrees. Its ideal fan-beam complementary angle is beta plus 180 degrees plus 2 gamma. The acquired complementary views immediately before and after that angle define two angular branches. In each branch, the direct-side and complementary-side detector-row candidates are merged, the closest candidate with z smaller than z0 and the closest candidate with z larger than z0 are selected over the ideal infinite helix, and their linear longitudinal weights are normalized to one with zero first moment about z0. The two branch kernels are then combined by the angular interpolation fraction. Equal-z ties share their endpoint weight equally as a neutral geometric convention. The configured slice-thickness rectangle is applied only after this acquisition-geometry kernel is assembled, using exact integration of its piecewise-constant cell representation. The direct-ray 0-to-360-degree full-scan comparator uses the original one-family nearest-bracketing rule. No fixed candidate support cutoff or scanner-specific redundancy weight is applied.
angleConvention: The diagram uses a model-relative tube angle beta with 0 degrees at the top and 360 degrees at the bottom. It is not a measured absolute tube angle. The drawn endpoint at 360 degrees closes the displayed helix period but is not double-counted in SSPz integration.
overlayConvention: The overlay samples 360 equally spaced relative reconstruction states within one table feed per rotation. All 360 configured-output profiles are rendered as 360 separate thin paths without state decimation, an overlaid pointwise summary curve, or a filled range. These are not 360 acquisitions or measured absolute tube angles. Every profile is peak-normalized and kept on its native z-minus-z0 coordinate without additional alignment. The linear center-shape view derives its symmetric horizontal domain from configured-output values at or above 10 percent of peak. The separate logarithmic tail view derives its domain from configured-output values at or above 0.1 percent. Off/on panels share a domain only within the same view role. The internal pre-thickness response is not exposed as a public SSPz or width result.
candidateDisplayConvention: The no-cone reference and cone-geometry-scaled conditions use the same candidate identities: all N detector-row centres in every displayed acquired view. The no-cone reference fixes the angle-dependent row-offset scale to one; it does not restrict the population to central rows or to configured-slice-thickness support. Section 2A thin detector-row-coloured trajectories denote this complete candidate pool without selection or weighting. Section 2B retains the same trajectories and overlays circles only at the nearest interpolation endpoints selected from that pool; marker intensity represents normalized linear interpolation weight, and marker count is not candidate-population size. Configured slice thickness T does not filter the pool or select endpoints; it is applied only after the acquisition-geometry kernel is assembled to form configured-output SSPz. The overview spans every turn containing a selected row-wise nearest smaller-z or larger-z endpoint over the inspected period plus one neighboring turn on either side and renders every detector row without row subsampling. The separate 180LI charts show the ideal complementary angular separation and its acquired-view bracket, the D-n-to-C-n and C-n-to-D-n-plus-one constrained spans in absolute helical acquisition order, and the merged all-candidate pair with its smaller-z and larger-z endpoints. The ideal helix is infinite; the displayed finite range is a reproducible view around the target plane, not the complete acquisition trajectory.
acquisitionGeometryFigureConvention: The Section 3C introductory figure is a pre-weight acquisition-geometry display for the currently inspected state. It shows a not-to-scale orthographic focal-spot helix, target plane, one direct acquired view, the two acquired complementary views bracketing the ideal beta plus 180 degrees plus 2 gamma angle, and every detector-row center mapped to the longitudinal line through the evaluation point. Nine representative row rays are drawn in the 3-D panel only for legibility; the adjacent longitudinal panel and numerical calculation retain all rows. A physical detector plane is not inferred because detector-to-isocenter distance is not an input. Color, opacity, and line width encode geometric role only. Circle and triangle markers identify candidates nearest the target plane for explanation; they do not assert use or weight. Schaller AAI h(z), weight normalization, filtering, and backprojection are not applied in this figure.
weightDisplayConvention: Candidate markers have a fixed size. Within each detector-row hue, color intensity from pale to dark represents the final normalized contribution after longitudinal and, for the 180LI path, angular interpolation. Coincident candidates share endpoint weight equally; this is a neutral geometric tie convention rather than a scanner redundancy weight.
allCandidateAxialSpreadConvention: For every direct acquired view beta, the candidate set contains all N detector-row centres in that direct view and all N row centres in each distinct acquired view immediately below and above the ideal complementary angle. A repeated lower-and-upper physical view is included only once, yielding 2N points for an exactly acquired complementary angle and 3N points otherwise. If z-k are the candidate positions, z-bar is their arithmetic mean, and M is their count, the displayed value is sqrt(sum((z-k minus z-bar) squared)/M) in millimetres. It uses no interpolation weight, nearest-candidate selection, support threshold, detector-row aperture variance, or configured slice thickness T. The value is invariant under a common longitudinal translation, so reconstruction-plane position s is not repeated as a second axis. The off/on curves use the same beta and millimetre axes.
internalCandidateAuditConvention: Weighted candidate moments and nonzero final-candidate counts remain available only as regression audits for the separate explanatory SSPz model. They are not displayed or relabelled as the pre-weight all-row geometry spread.
momentConvention: Every per-view final candidate kernel is normalized to total weight one. Its weighted center mu and second central moment M2 include both candidate-center dispersion and each uniform row aperture's intrinsic variance a-squared over 12. Longitudinal linear interpolation targets zero first moment about z0. With equal direct-view weights, the view-averaged pre-thickness variance is mean-view M2. The centered uniform configured-thickness rectangle adds T-squared over 12, so the explanatory model's analytic identity is sigma-configured-squared equals mean-view M2 plus T-squared over 12. The numerical configured-output standard deviation is audited against this identity.
numericalRasterizationConvention: For each entered condition, the finite uniform z grid is shared across relative reconstruction states and cone conditions. The requested count is a minimum; the implementation targets cell width no larger than the smaller of row width over 16 and configured thickness T over 64, raises the count to an odd value so one cell center is exactly z equals zero, and caps it at 65,535 with an explicit cap-hit audit flag. Every unit-area rectangular candidate response is deposited as exact overlap length with each intersected cell divided by aperture width and cell width; no rectangle endpoint is rounded to an integer bin. The configured-thickness moving rectangle integrates the piecewise-constant cell profile with exact fractional overlap at both window boundaries. This conserves area for contained supports and removes endpoint-bin centroid bias while retaining the declared finite-grid, piecewise-constant approximation.
complementaryPairConvention: The primary 180LI SSPz path is exact only within the declared idealized acquisition model. Its continuous complementary angle uses the second intersection of the source-to-evaluation-point line with the source orbit. For each acquired angular neighbor, all direct-side and complementary-side detector-row samples are merged and the adjacent candidates around z0 are used, allowing DD, DC, CD, or CC types while retaining equal-distance ties and exact matches. The two branch kernels are combined by the ideal angle's linear fraction between the acquired neighbors. The absolute-order D-n-to-C-n and C-n-to-D-n-plus-one spans remain separate diagnostics and are not averaged as an unvalidated redundancy rule. Scanner-specific detector-channel interpolation, redundancy weights, cone-beam weights, z filtering, and backprojection remain outside scope.
